headline: AI-chip rout: CRDO -10.5%, QCOM/ADI -8%, NXPI/KEYS -7.6% on SK Hynix HBM4 slowdown + Broadcom capex miss; CAT -5.5% as tariff headwinds materialize. CWAN merger-arb closed June 25 at $24.55 — resolved. Hyperscaler late-July prints are next key signal.

Persisting AI-chip rout (Friday June 26 close, pre-market Monday). LRCX and MRVL escalated to RED via thesis cross-check — WFE cyclicality and AI capex moderation risks now materializing. CAT improving: tariff estimate revised down to $2.2-2.4B, pre-market bounce +1.16%. CRDO stabilized. QCOM sell-off continuing. Hyperscaler late-July earnings window is primary forward risk.

AEM new RED — Q2 2026 gold crash -14% ($4,861→$4,040/oz, steepest quarterly decline on record) directly matches thesis key_risk #1; escalated AMBER→RED. MARA/HUT new AMBER on crypto-sector weakness and Q1 EPS miss. STLD new AMBER on Q2 guidance miss and margin compression. LRCX recovery (+4.88%) on Micron blowout — downgraded RED→AMBER. KEYS stabilizing — downgraded RED→AMBER. CAT tariff risk improving — resolved GREEN. ADI fully recovered — resolved GREEN. MRVL/CRDO/QCOM persisting RED. Hyperscaler late-July earnings window (MSFT July 29) remains primary macro catalyst for 8 AI-infrastructure holdings.

Broad AI-chip rebound accelerating: CRDO +10.7%, AMD +7.6%, MRVL +7.1%, LRCX +5.5% (resolved GREEN), TSM +4.9%. QCOM sole persisting RED (memory shortage, 4th session). New AMBER: SYK -4.8% (Russell index removal + ex-div + bearish valuation report, echoes valuation key_risk) and COIN -3.6% (crypto rout, Bitcoin sub-$60k, record ETF outflows — same theme pressuring MARA/HUT). STLD resolved GREEN — Q2 guidance actually shows sequential improvement, correcting the 06-30 margin-compression read. Hyperscaler earnings watch (MSFT 7/29) moved from active AMBER flag to calendar, 28 days out.

Broad AI-infrastructure selloff on a CNBC-confirmed report that Meta may rent out excess AI compute capacity, reviving oversupply fears: LRCX -9.72%, MRVL -8.5%, TSM -6.94%, AMD -6.83% all new/persisting RED, each matching a documented AI-capex-deceleration key_risk. HUT -8.35% escalated to RED as bitcoin hit a 21-month low (Bloomberg). CRDO -4.78% persists RED on the same AI-capex thesis link. CAT -6.71% and TOL -4.39% re-emerge AMBER on tariff/rate-cyclicality themes, though the specific day's catalysts are not yet tier-1 confirmed. AEM and QCOM downgraded RED→AMBER as gold and QCOM price action stabilize. DVN's guidance-suspension key_risk is resolved (Devon issued formal 2026 production guidance post-merger). CWAN roster issue persists unresolved for a third run. TSM's July 16 earnings print (2 weeks out) added to the AI-capex calendar watch.

AEM new RED on a tier-1-confirmed operational event (Barnat pit wall movement at Canadian Malartic, mining suspended, 60-80koz H2 guidance cut). MARA and KEYS escalated AMBER→RED on renewed declines (-7.47%, -6.50%). LRCX/MRVL/CRDO/HUT persist RED on the ongoing AI-capex-oversupply and crypto-weakness themes. AMD and TSM's price flags cooled (RED→AMBER/resolved) even as the underlying AI-capex story continues; TSM's July 16 earnings print is now a 2-week calendar watch item. GPC +12.91% on a Bloomberg-reported O'Reilly bid for its NAPA auto-parts unit — unconfirmed rumor stage, informational only. CWAN roster issue persists a fourth run.

No new trading session — markets closed 2026-07-03 (Independence Day observed) and 2026-07-04/05 (weekend); the data drop is unchanged from Friday's read (last session 2026-07-02). All flags below are carried forward unchanged: AEM (Malartic/Barnat guidance cut), LRCX/MRVL/CRDO/HUT/MARA/KEYS (AI-capex-oversupply + crypto-weakness rout) remain RED; AMD/QCOM remain AMBER. CWAN's roster issue is now time-critical — NYSE delisting takes effect at Monday's (2026-07-06) open. Next new data expected at Monday pre-market.

No new trading session — markets have been closed since 2026-07-02 (Independence Day observed 7/3, weekend 7/4-7/5); data drop is unchanged from Thursday's close. All 7 price-based RED flags (AEM, LRCX, MRVL, HUT, MARA, KEYS, CRDO) and 2 AMBER (AMD, QCOM) carry forward unchanged. New this run: FTNT flagged AMBER for the FortiBleed credential-exposure campaign (CISA alert, ~86,600 devices, active ransomware staging) — not yet reflected in price or analyst grades, but a first-time flag for the desk. Two new informational items: LMT reportedly a frontrunner for an ~$3.5B Ultra Maritime acquisition (unconfirmed by LMT), and COIN named in a multi-firm 'Open USD' stablecoin consortium (secondary-sourced). CWAN roster issue is now maximally time-critical — this is the final read before NYSE delisting takes effect at tomorrow's (2026-07-06) open, unresolved for a sixth straight run. Next new price data expected Monday pre-market.

No new trading session since Thursday 2026-07-02 (Friday 7/3 was a full-day Independence Day market holiday; this is a pre-market read ahead of today's open) — all 7 RED (AEM, LRCX, MRVL, HUT, MARA, KEYS, CRDO) and 3 AMBER (AMD, QCOM, FTNT) carry forward unchanged on price. The headline item this run is CWAN: NYSE's Form 25-NSE delisting is now confirmed effective at today's open, and portfolios.json still hasn't been corrected — this is the 7th straight run flagging it, and the deadline the desk was watching has now passed. FortiBleed reporting has advanced from a generic credential-exposure alert to a confirmed link with active INC/Lynx ransomware operations. TSM's July 16 earnings now falls inside the 2-week hyperscaler-capex watch window.

First new trading session (Mon 2026-07-06) since Thursday 7/2 brought a broad risk-on rally — a weaker-than-expected June jobs report (57K vs ~113K forecast) cooled Fed rate-hike fears and reversed most of the prior AI-capex-fear chip selloff. CRDO (+9.71%, fresh Evercore/Stifel/BofA upgrades) and AMD (+6.56%, Goldman PT to $640) are RESOLVED to green. LRCX, MRVL, HUT, MARA and KEYS all downgrade RED→AMBER on stabilization/recovery with no new negative catalyst (though LRCX notably didn't participate in the rally, and its CEO disclosed an $11.7M stock sale). AEM is now the lone RED: no new operational news, but analysts split (Jefferies upgrade vs UBS cut) while the Barnat guidance-cut risk stays open until the formal Q2 update on 7/29. QCOM holds AMBER as Citi's new 30-day downside catalyst watch (citing a ~30% Xiaomi 2026 shipment-forecast cut) gives the first concrete confirmation of the already-flagged Chinese-handset-softness risk. FTNT holds AMBER, unchanged. Headline roster item: CWAN is now fully deregistered (Form 15-12G filed 7/6) yet still sits in portfolios.json's growth sleeve — 8th consecutive run flagging this. LMT's Ultra Maritime interest converted from rumor to a signed $3.45B definitive agreement.

AI-capex-fear selloff resumed hard on the 7/7 session: Samsung's Q2 profit beat (surpassing NVDA and Apple) still missed sky-high AI-demand expectations, triggering a broad chip/AI-infrastructure re-rating on capex-durability doubts. MRVL -7.42%, CRDO -7.14%, LRCX -6.78% and AMD -6.57% all escalate/re-escalate to RED — a direct, tier-1-confirmed materialization of each name's already-flagged 'AI capex moderation / multiple compression' key_risk (CRDO and AMD had just resolved to green on 7/6 analyst upgrades — a sharp one-day whipsaw). AEM remains the lone persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk still unresolved; formal update due 7/29). HUT (-6.83%) and MARA (-6.73%) fell in sympathy with the AI-infrastructure trade despite Bitcoin itself holding steady (~$61.8k-63.7k) — a sentiment-correlation move, not a fresh BTC-price-exposure confirmation, so held at AMBER rather than RED. TSM (-4.22%), KEYS (-3.44%), HOOD (-3.98%), COIN (-3.24%), CAT (-3.04%, tariff overhang), and SUPV (-3.6%, no name-specific catalyst found) round out a wide AMBER band on a broadly risk-off tape (QQQ -1.83% vs SPY -0.47%). Notable divergence: NVDA (+0.71%) decoupled entirely from the memory/equipment-led selloff. CWAN roster issue persists a 9th consecutive run.

Sharp whipsaw reversal one session later (7/8): the chip/AI-infrastructure names that re-escalated to RED on 7/7's Samsung-driven selloff (MRVL, CRDO, LRCX, AMD) round-tripped back to green, alongside a broad semiconductor rally (NVDA, NXPI, QCOM, ADI, KEYS all up). New RED: SYF -9.64%, the sleeve's worst single-day move, on tier-1-confirmed (CNBC) 30-year Treasury yields holding above 5% pressuring consumer-finance funding costs ahead of SYF's 7/21 earnings — a direct materialization of its 'net interest margin pressure from higher funding costs' key_risk. AEM remains the lone persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk still unresolved, formal update due 7/29, -3.65% today with no fresh catalyst). New/upgraded AMBER band: TOL -3.74% (margin compression, elevated mortgage-rate sensitivity), GPC -3.08% (O'Reilly's confirmed $10B NAPA bid still undecided, Bloomberg reports a decision possible 'late summer'), FCX -3.01% (second consecutive ~-3% session, no confirmed catalyst), CHD -2.84%, COIN -2.47% (crypto-tape softness — ETHA -2.74% and IBIT -2.48% also down), SUPV -2.2% (Argentina macro, ongoing), FTNT -1.21% (FortiBleed reporting still static). On the positive side: HUT +9.82% on $7.5B in confirmed project financing plus a wave of analyst price-target increases (Rosenblatt, B. Riley, Jefferies, KBW); VLO +6.28% on strong refining crack spreads ahead of its 7/30 print. CWAN roster issue persists a 10th consecutive run. TSM's 7/16 earnings (confirmed via TSMC investor relations) falls inside the 2-week hyperscaler-capex calendar watch.

Quiet-to-firm session overall (2 RED, 5 AMBER, rest calm/positive). New RED: STLD -2.96%, a continuation of its Q2 guidance cut (aluminum write-down) directly matching its flagged steel-price-cyclicality/earnings-swing risk. AEM remains the lone persisting RED — Barnat pit incident now quantified at 60-80k oz of lost 2H2026 production, formal guidance update still due 7/29 (today's +2.89% is a technical bounce, not a resolution). New macro watch item: Strait of Hormuz shipping has 'ground to a halt' amid renewed US-Iran fighting (tier-1: CNBC, Al Jazeera, NBC) — oil prices elevated but so far orderly; flagged AMBER as a live cross-sleeve risk to the energy names (DVN, VLO, OKE, CVX, CNX) and broader market sentiment, not yet a confirmed thesis break. NTR -3.34% (today's largest decline) continues to drift on recent analyst target cuts (Morgan Stanley $93→$81, UBS Sell) with no fresh single-day catalyst found. DVN -2.93% on no specific news, consistent with recent PT trims (Truist, Morgan Stanley) and energy-sector chop. SYF partially recovered (+4.87%) from yesterday's -9.64% rate-driven plunge but remains well below its pre-selloff level with 7/21 earnings approaching — held at AMBER, not fully resolved. Broad chip/AI-infrastructure rally (LRCX +5.97%, AMD +5.61%, MRVL +5.02%, FCX +5.25%) on SK Hynix's oversubscribed Nasdaq ADR debut and Micron's $3B US supply-chain investment — resolves/extends the green trend from 7/9. MARA +9.91% on broader crypto-linked strength. CWAN roster issue persists an 11th consecutive run — still uncorrected.

Data-quality note: today's read is built on a fresh on-demand Risk Data Drop dispatch, since the file sitting in the repo was a Friday pre-market snapshot (still showing Thursday's close) and markets are closed today (Saturday) with no scheduled weekday refresh — the dispatch pulled Friday 7/10's actual settled close, so as_of_session is now correctly 2026-07-10. AEM remains the lone persisting RED — Barnat pit production-cut risk still unresolved, formal guidance update due 7/29, no change this run. STLD downgraded RED→AMBER on a +2.92% partial rebound with no new negative news; the underlying guidance-cut thesis risk stays open, not worsening. New AMBER: a broad, catalyst-less Growth-sleeve pullback — MARA -4.58%, HUT -3.85%, FTNT -3.78%, HRMY -3.66%, MRVL -3.08%, CRDO -2.98%, HOOD -2.78% — while SPY/QQQ were flat-to-up (+0.45%/+0.33%), reading as sector-specific profit-taking after last week's AI-chip/crypto rally rather than a market-wide risk-off move; MARA/HUT weakness is consistent with Bitcoin's ongoing monthly downtrend (-18% MTD) even as BTC bounced modestly in the last 24h. Strait of Hormuz shipping macro watch persists AMBER — Bloomberg (7/9) confirms traffic is still near-standstill amid the resumed US-Iran fighting, no change since last run. SYF persists AMBER, continuing its recovery (+1.17%) with 7/21 earnings the open catalyst. NTR, DVN, and SUPV all resolved to GREEN on rebounds (SUPV +5.92%) with no fresh negative catalyst found for any of the three. CWAN roster issue persists a 12th consecutive run, still uncorrected in portfolios.json. TSM's 7/16 earnings remains the near-term hyperscaler-capex calendar watch.

Second consecutive weekend read off the same Friday 7/10 close — no new trading session since Friday, and today's on-demand Risk Data Drop dispatch reproduced identical prices/moves to yesterday's Saturday read (SPY +0.45%, QQQ +0.33%, NVDA +4.09%, etc. all match Friday's close exactly). Targeted web search this run (AEM, SYF, CWAN, Strait of Hormuz, MARA/HUT, FTNT, TSM) found no material weekend developments beyond what was already known — all flags held at unchanged severity. AEM remains the lone persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk, formal update due 7/29, unchanged). STLD holds AMBER (guidance-cut thesis risk open, not worsening after Friday's rebound). Broad catalyst-less Growth-sleeve pullback (MARA -4.58%, HUT -3.85%, FTNT -3.78%, HRMY -3.66%, MRVL -3.08%, CRDO -2.98%, HOOD -2.78%) persists AMBER, still unconfirmed by any new tier-1 catalyst. Strait of Hormuz shipping macro watch persists AMBER — confirmed still near-standstill via Al Jazeera/UN News, no change since 7/10. SYF persists AMBER into 7/21 earnings (9 days out). TSM's 7/16 hyperscaler-capex print is now 4 days out, inside the standing capex-watch window. CWAN roster issue persists a 13th consecutive run, still uncorrected in portfolios.json.

New RED this run: Strait of Hormuz conflict escalated over the weekend (fresh US-Iran airstrikes), Brent/WTI up 6-7% on the week to the high-$70s/low-$80s, and Nasdaq futures are down ~0.9% pre-open Monday — none of this is reflected yet in the pre-market data drop (still pricing Friday 7/10's close), so the energy sleeve (DVN, VLO, OKE, CVX, CNX) and broader risk tone could gap at today's open. AEM remains the other persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk, formal update due 7/29, unchanged). STLD holds AMBER (guidance-cut thesis risk still open despite Friday's rebound). Growth-sleeve pullback (MARA, HUT, FTNT, HRMY, MRVL, CRDO, HOOD) persists AMBER, still no confirmed name-specific catalyst beyond the broader risk-off/Bitcoin-drawdown backdrop. SYF persists AMBER into 7/21 earnings (8 days out). TSM's 7/16 hyperscaler-capex print is now 3 days out. Also on deck this week: bank earnings and June CPI on Tuesday (no direct held-name overlap, but sets the macro tone). CWAN roster issue persists a 14th consecutive run, still uncorrected in portfolios.json.

New RED: AI-capex-durability selloff re-erupted across the chip/AI-infrastructure complex (CRDO -8.18%, MRVL -7.78%, LRCX -5.79%, AMD -4.33%, NVDA -3.56%, TSM -2.96%) on SK Hynix HBM-expansion-slowdown reports plus growing Street skepticism about AI capex ROI — this is the same thesis-linked pattern that has whipsawed this cluster RED/AMBER/green repeatedly since late June, and it matches each name's stated valuation/capex-deceleration key_risk almost verbatim. Separately, the Hormuz macro RED escalated further and is now confirmed in price: US-Iran strikes are in a third consecutive night, the ceasefire has fractured, Trump has reinstated an Iran shipping blockade and proposed a 20% Hormuz transit toll, Brent is above $87 (+4.45% today, +9.6% Monday) and WTI is near $81 — the book's energy sleeve is rallying hard in response (VLO +5.41%, DVN +3.52%, CVX +3.33%, OKE +2.57%). The same energy shock is pushing Fed rate-HIKE odds higher (September hike probability near 76%, up from 57% a week ago) ahead of today's 8:30am CPI print and the start of bank earnings (JPM/GS/WFC/C). AEM holds as the third persisting RED (Barnat guidance-cut risk unresolved, formal update due 7/29). STLD holds AMBER (guidance-cut thesis unresolved despite the rebound continuing, +2.51% today; Q2 earnings now confirmed for release after close 7/20 with a 7/21 call). Growth-sleeve digital-asset names persist AMBER (MARA -3.29%, HUT -2.96%, HRMY -3.53%, alongside IBIT -2.71%/ETHA -1.04%) — FTNT has decoupled positively (+1.99%) and drops out of this flag. SYF persists AMBER into 7/21 earnings (7 days out). TSM's 7/16 hyperscaler-capex print is now 2 days out and directly in play given today's move. CWAN roster issue persists a 15th consecutive run, still uncorrected in portfolios.json.

AI-capex/HBM-linked selloff persists in the chip complex (MRVL -7.31%, CRDO -3.99%, AMD -3.53%, LRCX -3.06%) on continued SK Hynix HBM-ramp-slip and Chinese memory-glut (CXMT) fallout — but this reads as a differentiated, memory/equipment-specific re-rating rather than a broad AI-capex scare: TSM's Q2 print released today was a blowout (record profit, AI/HPC now 66% of revenue, analyst StrongBuys rose 11→13) and NVDA held flat, both barometers of underlying accelerator demand. Hormuz macro RED escalates further — ceasefire declared 'over' by Trump, a third+ round of US strikes hit Iranian missile sites, and reports say the US is weighing seizing Kharg Island (Iran's main oil export terminal), which would be a major escalation; Brent is consolidating near a one-month high (~$85) after giving back a third of Wednesday's spike, and the book's energy names pulled back in sympathy (VLO -2.67%, DVN -1.08%, OKE -1.07%) after Wednesday's rally — read as digestion, not thesis reversal, given oil remains elevated and the conflict is intensifying. AEM persists RED (Nunavut/Barnat-area guidance risk unresolved, formal update still due 7/29). STLD and SYF persist AMBER into confirmed earnings (7/20 AMC and 7/21 BMO respectively). Digital-asset sleeve (MARA +1.07%, HUT +4.70%, HRMY +0.24%, alongside IBIT +0.60%/ETHA +2.44%) resolves to GREEN on a broad-based rebound with no negative catalyst, dropping out of AMBER. CWAN roster-integrity issue persists a 16th consecutive run, still uncorrected in portfolios.json.

Two concurrent shocks hitting the book: (1) an AI-capex-sustainability selloff after TSMC raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B, hitting MRVL -8.6% (persisting RED, -31% over the month), CRDO -8.1% (persisting RED), AMD -5.2% and LRCX -4.3% (both AMBER); (2) Bitcoin's slide toward $60K on persistent spot-ETF outflows, hitting HUT -10.7% and MARA -6.8% (both escalated to RED on direct thesis match) and HOOD -8.2% (new RED). CWAN roster-integrity flag is now unresolved for a 3rd consecutive run — still listed in portfolios.json 22 days after delisting. Also note: a 17-day gap since the last Sentinel run (06-30 → 07-17) means several of today's reads are first looks, not continuous tracking. One bright spot: ABT +10.7% on a Q2 beat-and-raise, and the STLD margin-compression AMBER from 06-30 appears to have been wrong — STLD's own July guidance shows margin expansion, not compression; downgrading to resolved/green.

MARA (-6.47%) and HOOD (-5.76%) both extend a second straight session of outsized declines against Friday's broad selloff (SPY -1.0%, QQQ -1.5% on a chip-sector rout tied to a new Chinese AI model plus US-Iran tensions) — MARA persisting RED on its Bitcoin-derivative thesis risk, HOOD persisting RED after closing below $100 on Bloomberg-reported credit-card ABS scrutiny. New AMBER: SYK -3.44% (reverses Thursday's dividend-raise bounce on resurfacing Q2 cyber-recovery concerns, thesis-linked), FAST -2.57% (continuing to digest its July 14 gross-margin miss, thesis-linked), TOL -3.19% (swept into rate-sensitive housing weakness despite bullish analyst calls). CRDO downgraded RED→AMBER as Friday's AI-capex rout largely stabilized; HUT, MRVL, AMD, QCOM, VST, SUPV and COIN all resolved to green. VLO +3.11% led gainers on Iran-tension-driven crack spreads; ABT +1.91% extends its beat-and-raise strength. CWAN roster-integrity flag unresolved for a 4th consecutive run. Next catalyst: GOOG earnings 2026-07-22, first hyperscaler capex read of the season.

Weekend escalation in the US-Iran war (2 US troop deaths in Jordan, 8th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran, air-raid sirens in Bahrain) is the dominant new development — markets have been closed since Friday and have not priced it in; crude above $82/bbl, a one-month high. Energy sleeve (VLO, CVX, OKE, DVN, CNX) sits on the tailwind side; broader risk sentiment is the headwind into Monday's open. Friday's session itself carries forward unchanged: MARA (-6.47%) and HOOD (-5.76%) remain persisting RED on thesis-linked risk (Bitcoin-derivative exposure; thin-margin-of-safety credit scrutiny) though weekend Bitcoin action was mildly positive (+1.3% to ~$64.8K). SYK, TOL, CRDO, FAST, LRCX persist AMBER, all thesis- or sector-linked, none escalating. CWAN roster-integrity flag remains unresolved (24 days since deal close). Next catalyst: GOOG earnings 2026-07-22 (Tue) — first hyperscaler capex read of the season, 3 days out.

No new equity session yet (markets open later today) but two names carry fresh, material catalysts into the open: Morgan Stanley cut its MARA price target to $5.50 (from $7, Underweight maintained), and HOOD's consumer-credit expansion (up to $500M in asset-backed securities) continues to draw scrutiny with shares down ~9% on the week toward the $100 level. The Iran war has escalated further overnight — cumulative US troop deaths now reported at 17, a 9th consecutive night of US strikes, and Brent crude briefly topped $90/bbl before easing to $88.54 — a continuing tailwind for the energy sleeve (VLO, CVX, OKE, DVN, CNX) and a geopolitical overhang for broader risk sentiment. GOOG's Q2 earnings (Wed 2026-07-22, first hyperscaler capex read) is now 2 days out. CWAN roster-integrity flag remains unresolved for a 26th day.

MARA (+8.97%) and HOOD (flat) both downgrade RED->AMBER as this week's negative catalysts fade -- MARA on a new Texas AI/HPC power deal, HOOD on simple stabilization near $100. HUT is the standout, +10.45% on a $9.8B AI lease that fully commercializes its Beacon Point campus -- a thesis catalyst materializing ahead of schedule. CRDO (+5.0%) resolves to green as the AI-capex-rout unwind continues alongside MRVL (+3.3%). New: STLD -2.23% on a Q2 print showing an aluminum-segment impairment overshadowing record steel shipments. The US-Iran conflict remains the one portfolio-level RED -- unresolved, oil near $89/bbl -- ahead of GOOG's Q2 print tomorrow (07-22), the season's first hyperscaler-capex read. CWAN roster-integrity flag remains unresolved for a 27th day.

Broad risk-on session: crypto-adjacent names (COIN +9.5%, HOOD +7.2%) surge on CLARITY Act Senate momentum, resolving HOOD's regulatory-risk AMBER to green; AMD +8.1% on the Microsoft Azure Helios deployment deal into today's Advancing AI 2026 event; AI-chip/data-center names (MRVL, FCX, TSM, CRDO, LRCX) rally in sympathy ahead of GOOG's Q2 print after today's close -- the season's first hyperscaler-capex read. Meanwhile dividend-sleeve defensives rotated lower: GPC fell despite a Q2 beat on cautious H2 guidance citing Iran-conflict cost pressure (new AMBER, thesis-linked), ADP -3.6% with no same-day catalyst confirmed by a tier-1 source (new AMBER), and ATAT hit a fresh 52-week low (new AMBER). The US-Iran conflict remains the one portfolio-level RED -- not de-escalating, Brent near $92 with Trump threatening broader strikes. CWAN roster-integrity flag unresolved for a 28th day.

Iran conflict sharply escalates -- oil tankers struck off Saudi Arabia, Houthis claim Red Sea attacks, Iran's IRGC reports a mined-route tanker explosion near the Strait of Hormuz, and the US completed a 12th consecutive night of strikes; Brent topped $98.44 (+4.6%) and WTI ~$90, the highest since May/June -- remains the sole portfolio-level RED, still not de-escalating. GOOG's Q2 print landed with revenue/EPS beats but a large capex raise ($195-205B FY guide, up from $180-190B) that punished GOOG itself (negative free cash flow for the first time) -- the desk's AI-infra suppliers read it constructively instead (NVDA +2.3%, CRDO +2.0%, MRVL +1.5%, AMD +1.4%, TSM/LRCX roughly flat), resolving the standing hyperscaler-capex watch favorably. A reversal day for last week's high-flyers: COIN (-5.5%) and HRMY (-5.3%) both give back their prior-session pops with no new tier-1-confirmed catalyst identified; TEL (-4.2%) extends Tuesday's ~7% post-acquisition-announcement slide (Astrodyne TDI, $1.4B) despite a record Q3 beat -- a capital-allocation reaction, not a fundamental miss. FCX (+3.9%) reported Q2 results this morning and continues recovering from the earlier Grasberg-delay overhang. CWAN roster-integrity flag unresolved for a 29th day.

Iran conflict escalates further overnight -- Brent crosses $100/bbl for the first time this cycle -- remains the sole macro RED alongside the 30-day-unresolved CWAN roster flag. Defense and diagnostics deliver the day's real news: LMT +10.3% on a Q2 beat, raised guidance, and a record $230B backlog anchored by the $35B THAAD contract (a listed key catalyst materializing), and DGX +8.3% on a Q2 beat with raised full-year guidance. HUT +7.1% on a new $9.8B Beacon Point AI-lease, pulling its contracted-revenue thesis catalyst forward. SUPV -5.7% with no tier-1-confirmed catalyst identified. QCOM -2.5% for a second straight down day amid chip-sector AI-demand-durability jitters ahead of its 07-29 print. Crypto-linked names stayed soft (COIN -3.0%, HOOD -2.8%) as Bitcoin eased toward $65K; gold and copper both retraced (AEM -2.0%, FCX -2.3%) on oil-driven rate-hike repricing, not name-specific news. AMD's 08-04 print enters the ~2-week hyperscaler-capex watch window.

25-day monitoring gap since last run (2026-06-30). CWAN roster issue unresolved (delisted, still in portfolios.json). 5 RED: CRDO/MRVL/QCOM/LRCX/AEM all persisting or re-escalating thesis-matched risks (valuation compression, hyperscaler concentration, memory shortage, gold price). SSNC +10.3% on Q2 beat/raise. Hyperscaler capex season underway — GOOGL raised capex to $195-205B (7/22); MSFT/META report 7/29, AMZN 7/30.

Coverage gap: no Sentinel run for 26 days (last: 2026-06-30).
